key_insight: The paper proves global linear convergence of full-batch and minibatch Adam for sufficiently wide two-layer networks, including physics-informed networks solving the Poisson equation.
engineering_relevance: The results provide theoretical guidance on how network width, Adam parameters, and minibatch size affect reliable loss reduction in PINN training.
method: Construct a Lyapunov function to control full-batch Adam’s momentum history.
Analyze minibatch Adam using exact virtual iterates, gradient–preconditioner dependence, and second-moment concentration bounds.
Extend convergence guarantees to Poisson PINNs with separately sampled interior and boundary points.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical geometric loss-decay guarantees, with minibatch results in restricted expectation on a high-probability event; no empirical benchmarks are described.
watch_item: Guarantees require sufficiently wide two-layer networks and explicit parameter conditions, so they do not automatically extend to practical deep PINNs or other PDEs.
paper_title: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
